overview: The ATtiny85 isn't a board at all — it's a bare 8-pin DIP microcontroller chip, small and cheap enough to leave embedded permanently in a tiny project where even a Pro Mini feels oversized. It has no onboard USB, no bootloader by default, and needs a separate programmer (an Arduino running as 'Arduino as ISP', or a USB programmer) to load code. In exchange you get an entire AVR microcontroller in a package smaller than a fingernail, popular in boards like the Digispark and in mass-produced blinking-light gadgets.
simpleSummary: A tiny, cheap chip-only microcontroller for projects too small to need a full Arduino.

specifications.clockSpeed: 1 MHz internal (up to 20 MHz with external crystal)
specifications.connector: None — requires an external ISP programmer

pinMap.name: PB5 (RESET)
pinMap.function: Reset pin; pulling LOW resets the chip. Can be reconfigured as a weak digital I/O pin at the cost of losing easy reprogramming.
pinMap.gotcha: Reconfiguring this as a GPIO pin makes the chip much harder to reprogram afterward — a common irreversible-feeling mistake for beginners.

pinMap.name: PB3 (XTAL1)
pinMap.function: General-purpose digital I/O, or external crystal input if using one.

pinMap.name: PB4 (XTAL2)
pinMap.function: General-purpose digital I/O, or external crystal input if using one.

pinMap.name: PB0 (MOSI)
pinMap.function: General-purpose digital I/O; used as MOSI during ISP programming.

pinMap.name: PB1 (MISO)
pinMap.function: General-purpose digital I/O; used as MISO during ISP programming.

pinMap.name: PB2 (SCK)
pinMap.function: General-purpose digital I/O; used as SCK during ISP programming.

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.gotcha: Only 5 usable I/O pins total — plan pin budget carefully before starting a project.

useCases.title: Blinking-light gadget
useCases.scenario: The classic use: a tiny standalone board (like a Digispark) running a simple LED pattern, sold as a complete cheap product.

useCases.title: Tiny USB gadget (Digispark)
useCases.scenario: The Digispark board adds USB via software emulation, letting the ATtiny85 act as a simple USB device.

useCases.title: Embedded sensor trigger
useCases.scenario: Permanently embed in a project that just needs to read one sensor and flip one output (e.g. a moisture-triggered LED).

commonlyPairedWith: Arduino Uno (used as an ISP programmer)
oftenConfusedWith: Arduino Pro Mini (has far more pins and easy Serial debugging)
oftenUpgradedTo: Arduino Pro Mini (when 5 pins isn't enough)
